# Cost Deck

> Cost Deck is an open-source (Apache 2.0) Kubernetes FinOps operator. It shows what every namespace, team, GPU and LLM token costs, scales idle non-production environments and the cloud databases behind them to zero on schedules, and right-sizes workloads with a guard that rolls back or as a pull request. One operator in your cluster runs the dashboard, a REST API and an MCP server; there is no external service and no paid tier.

- Requirements: Kubernetes 1.26 or newer, Helm 3.8 or newer, metrics-server. VictoriaMetrics or any Prometheus-compatible API adds history, throttling and better advice.
- Install: `helm upgrade --install costdeck-operator oci://ghcr.io/migalsp/costdeck/charts/costdeck-operator --namespace costdeck --create-namespace`
- Sign in: `kubectl port-forward -n costdeck svc/costdeck-operator-api 8082:8082`, open http://localhost:8082 as user `costdeck`; the password is in the Secret `costdeck-operator-admin-credentials`.
- MCP: Streamable HTTP at `https://<your-costdeck-host>/mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer cdk_...` (tokens from Settings > API tokens; a viewer token gives read-only tools). Works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients.
- REST API: OpenAPI at `/api/openapi.yaml` and `/api/openapi.json` on your installation.
- Changes it makes: replica counts (the original is kept on the workload), CronJob suspension, KEDA pausing; sleep-page routes and GitOps pausing only if enabled. It never touches nodes. A namespace with no schedule is never scaled down. Applying right-sizing is off until an admin turns it on.
- Cloud resources on the same schedules: AWS Aurora and EC2, Azure VMs and flexible servers, Google Cloud SQL and Compute Engine.
- Not covered: node autoscaling, reserved instances and savings plans, costs outside Kubernetes and the resources its schedules stop.
